suggested_iss.title: KS-005 TLDR: "Two inconsistent" vs section body + JSON "three inconsistent" (three values enumerated)
suggested_iss.description: The Test 5 (Eclipse 2026) ks-tldr paragraph in data/sections.json[part5].html reads 'Two inconsistent dome values (−17 to −21, −28.9 nT) undermine the claimed precision.' Two internally-adjacent surfaces contradict this: (a) the same section's detail-body paragraph (~500 chars later, same <details> block) reads 'Plugged in, the predicted dips at Ebro are reported in the dome\'s own documents as three inconsistent values — −17 to −21, −28.9, and −29.1 nT — which already undermines the claimed precision.' (b) the summary table row for KS-005 in the same section reads 'Chapman mechanism (1933) predicts same range; three inconsistent numbers'. And (c) data/kill-shots.json:KS-005.our_finding reads 'Three inconsistent dome values (−17 to −21, −28.9, −29.1 nT) undermine claimed precision.' All three-value surfaces enumerate three concrete values (−17 to −21, −28.9, −29.1). Only the TLDR count and enumeration is off. Not a scientific error (the argument is unchanged whether the count is two or three); a within-section consistency drift.

kernel_of_truth: The eclipse cluster is genuinely the most methodologically careful item in the dome registry (nine INTERMAGNET stations, per-station magnitudes, git pre-registration). Our review acknowledges this explicitly in the Test 5 detail body. The TLDR's undercount of the dome's own documentation inconsistencies runs OPPOSITE to the drift class we would normally worry about — it makes the dome look slightly LESS internally inconsistent than the evidence supports, not more. So this is a minor honesty-tightening, not a rhetorical amplification.
counter_argument: A reader could argue the TLDR reasonably summarizes the dome's two published magnitude estimates (the −17-21 range and the −28.9 nT central value) and omits the −29.1 nT variant as a rounding-difference sibling. However the detail body, the summary table row, AND the kill-shots.json all treat the three values as distinct 'inconsistent' entries. The TLDR should track the detail rather than pre-selecting a subset without saying so. If a shorter TLDR is preferred, drop a value from the detail body too — the current asymmetry is the bug.
